chunks: As for what Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn al-Husayn and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: I enter with these people in the maghrib salat, and they hurry me before I can give the adhan and iqamah, so I do not recite anything, until when they perform ruku', I perform ruku' with them. Will that suffice for me? He said: Yes.

So the correct understanding of his statement, "I do not recite," is that it is carried upon what is additional to al-Hamd, because the recitation of al-Hamd is indispensable. What indicates that is that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, the narrator of this hadith, narrated this same incident itself and said: I am not able to recite what is additional to al-Hamd, so he said to him: Yes.

key_terms.أُؤَذِّنَ: to give the adhan before commencing salat
key_terms.أُقِيمَ: to pronounce the iqamah before salat
key_terms.الْحَمْدِ: Sūrat al-Hamd, whose recitation is treated as necessary here
key_terms.رَكَعُوا: they performed ruku' in the congregational movement
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib salat being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.يُجْزِينِي: to suffice or be valid for fulfilling the obligation

ai.seo_question: Does it suffice to join the ruku' in maghrib salat if I cannot recite fully behind one who is not to be followed?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the ruling of recitation in salat behind one who is not to be followed. The Imam عليه السلام affirms the sufficiency of joining in ruku', and the accompanying explanation clarifies that the omission is understood to apply to recitation beyond Sūrat al-Hamd, since al-Hamd itself is necessary.
